fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. The writer says, “…what is obsolete and aging will soon disappear.” He says it right after saying the new covenant made the first one obsolete. So the answer is right there in the verse: it will soon disappear.
That's the seat, baker. The writer says Jesus took His seat at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven. He is the high priest we really do have, seated in heaven.

A mountain does show up in this passage, but it's Moses' mountain in verse 5, where he was shown a pattern for the tabernacle. That has nothing to do with where Jesus sits. The writer says He sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven. Nice try, friend.

The writer says the opposite. Jesus ministers in the sanctuary and true tabernacle “…set up by the Lord, not by man.” No human builder set it up. My mustache can barely set up a cookie rack without a wobble.

That's right, baker. The writer says if Jesus were on earth, He would not be a priest. The reason given is that there are already priests here who offer gifts according to the law. Jesus has received a much more excellent ministry, the writer says in verse 6.
Yes, baker. The writer says the place where they serve is “…a copy and shadow of what is in heaven.” A copy points to the real thing without being the real thing. The real thing is what is in heaven.
That's it, baker. Moses, Israel's leader, was warned, “…make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.” The warning came when he was about to build the tabernacle.

Yes, baker. The writer says, “But God found fault with the people…” That's who God found fault with. Verse 7 adds that if the first covenant had been without fault, no place would have been sought for a second.
The prophets don't come up in this passage, friend. The writer says God found fault with the people. That's the word that fits the blank.
That's it, baker. God says, “I will put My laws in their minds and inscribe them on their hearts.” The laws go on the inside. I think that's the part that gets me every time.
A season would mean the sins are remembered for a time, and that's not what God says. He says He will remember their sins no more. “No more” leaves no season at all.

Two covenants sharing one counter sounds cozy, friend, but that's not the picture here. The writer says what is obsolete and aging will soon disappear. He says it right after saying that by speaking of a new covenant, He has made the first one obsolete. So the old doesn't stand beside the new, it disappears.
